items.title: GM Faces Safety Probe Over Engine-Failure Concerns in Nearly One Million Vehicles
items.summary: Federal auto-safety regulators are opening an investigation into nearly one million  General Motors  pickup trucks and sport-utility vehicles after receiving hundreds of reports of engine failures.  The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said Friday it was launching the probe into vehicles equipped with a particular GM V-8 engine that had already been the subject of an earlier recall.  The regulator has received nearly 500 complaints alleging engine failure in vehicles that had already been serviced under recall, including nearly two dozen that required complete engine replacements.

items.title: Walmart’s E-Commerce Sales Rise as Deliveries Accelerate
items.summary: Walmart said its U.S. e-commerce sales rose 24% in the second quarter, with more than 40% sales growth in deliveries fulfilled at its stores.  CEO  John Furner  said  Walmart  has now expanded deliveries of 30 minutes or less into 38 U.S. markets.  The number of units delivered in less than half an hour has doubled in the current quarter from a year ago, and 70% of all e-commerce orders are getting delivered on the same day or better, CFO  John David Rainey  said.

items.title: NHTSA opens probe into nearly 1 million GM pickups, SUVs over engine failure concerns
items.summary: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ‌said on Friday it has ‌opened a probe into 997,743 General Motors ​pickup trucks and SUVs over concerns related to engine failure. The vehicles include the Cadillac Escalade, Chevrolet ‌Silverado 1500 ⁠and GMC Yukon, among others, from model years 2021-2026 ⁠equipped with GM's L87 engines.
